title: Choose the visual world for manifesotrading.com
question: The roll assigned Site Hi-Vis. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Site Hi-Vis
options.lineage: EN ISO 20471 hi-vis vests and induction-stickered hard hats on Qatar tower sites
options.thesis: The website wears what the team wears on site: fluorescent yellow fabric, two silver retroreflective bands, the company name stencilled across the back, and hard-hat induction stickers that name every tower the team has been inducted onto.
options.viewport: A fluorescent-yellow field owns the upper half: MANIFESO stencilled huge in navy like the back of a vest, crossed by a silver reflective band carrying the three services. Below the band, a real photo of a technician at a rack. WhatsApp + call buttons sit in the band itself; project 'induction stickers' (Voya, R02, Al Wusail, Rawdatama) cluster on the right like a hard hat.
options.risk: Fluorescent yellow is loud; if the photos are not given calm navy and off-white room it turns into a safety poster.

raised.raise: Projects page is a ruled, fixed-column register (project · location · scope · year · status) where rows are the entities and columns never move.
Registration discipline: one fixed keyline grid that every photo and band snaps to, so the loud colour always lands in register.

options.label: Project Site Board
options.lineage: the signboard at every Qatar construction gate: Client / Consultant / Main Contractor / ELV Subcontractor
options.thesis: Every page is a site hoarding board: white aluminium panels with role bands, the project name huge, Manifeso named as the ELV subcontractor, partners as the stacked logo rows.
options.viewport: A hoarding-board header: role bands (ELV CONTRACTOR — MANIFESO) over a site photo, services as the board's scope lines.
options.risk: The strongest fit, and also the most familiar: close to what construction companies already ship.

options.label: Normalled Jackfield
options.thesis: Projects and services as numbered lanes on black glass tied by amber link lines, like a patch schedule.
options.viewport: Numbered lanes 01–48 with services as linked ports; photos framed in amber.
options.case: Fuses well with structured cabling — your audience knows patch panels by heart; loses on clarity for a contractor who just wants proof and a phone number.
options.risk: Reads as a dark 'tech' dashboard, close to the AI neon look you want to avoid.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.case: Contractors don't identify with a departures board.
options.kept: Fixed-column register: rows are projects, columns never move.

options.label: Ukiyo-e Registration
options.case: No connection to Qatar ELV contracting.
options.kept: Everything lands in register on one fixed keyline.

options.label: VHS Rental Wall
options.kept: Browse sideways: project photo strips scroll horizontally on phones.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean contractor site: white page, navy header, full-width photo hero, services row, project gallery, contact.
canonCard.viewport: Photo hero with headline and two buttons, services below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other contractor site in Doha.
